newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp - normalised dollar does not reflect EMU fears.
newsitem.headline: Krupp - normalised dollar does not reflect EMU fears.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Thursday that the normalisation of the dollar did not reflect market concerns about the launch of Europe's single currency.
"The fact that the dollar has normalised of late has nothing to do with the euro," Krupp told a conference on economic issues.
Krupp was responding to comments by another speaker who suggested that the mark has weakened because there were broad doubts that the euro will not be as stable as the mark.
Krupp noted that German yields were significantly below those of the United States.
"That does not support the flight of capital theory," he said. Krupp also said that the markets viewed the euro at the moment "as the opportunity of the future."
Krupp also dismissed talk of a possible delay to the start of European monetary union saying that there would be little point in this.
"How can a Europe with 14 small currencies survive for much longer?" he said. "What is the point in a delay?"
